This is a site page, not an area page: recip.html IS a listing feed — the site's reciprocal-listings search page, browser title "Search all South Surrey listings," headed "SEARCH ALL LISTINGS." It carries a paginated MLS® feed of Active listings held by other brokerages; it has no single geography, no single market, and no building list of its own — states that plainly and documents what the feed actually surfaces instead.
Streets, schools and getting around Recip

items.t: Boundaries: NONE apply as a market — a cross-area search feed has no single geography. At reading the feed carried a paginated MLS® feed ("1-12 / 310," 26 pages) of Active listings held by other brokerages, under an editorial intro headed "Explore every available property across South Surrey, Langley, and the Fraser Valley," with a second editorial section below the feed ("Homes for Sale Across South Surrey, Langley & Fraser Valley").

Feed geography as read: all 12 first-page cards are Surrey properties — Grandview Surrey (5), King George Corridor (3), Morgan Creek (2), Elgin Chantrell (1), Sunnyside Park Surrey (1) — that is, the South Surrey side of Surrey, matching the browser title "Search all South Surrey listings." The intro copy, however, describes the search as covering "South Surrey, Langley, White Rock, Cloverdale, and the Fraser Valley," and the below-feed editorial names Abbotsford and Chilliwack among the areas covered.
Where condo stock concentrates: nowhere on this page — the page concentrates nothing; it aggregates. No street or node is this page's own.

What each card shows: address, sub-area label, price, "Residential," Status: Active, MLS® number, bedrooms, bathrooms, floor area, the listing description text, any open-house times, and "Listed by" naming the listing brokerage — on the first page: SRS Westside Realty, LeHomes Realty Premier, Unilife Realty Inc., Macdonald Realty (Surrey/152), Angell, Hasman & Associates Realty Ltd., RE/MAX Colonial Pacific Realty, RE/MAX Crest Realty, Woodhouse Realty, Sutton Group-West Coast Realty, Real Broker and eXp Realty. No first-page card is listed by Jared's own brokerage — which is the point of a reciprocity feed: it surfaces participating firms' listings on Jared's site, and each card carries the Reciprocity logo.

What the detail layer shows: expanding a card repeats the listing with floor area in sq. ft. and m² and adds action links — "View photos," "Schedule viewing / Email," "Send listing," "View on map," "Mortgage calculator" — beside a Jared Gibbons / Royal LePage Little Oak Realty contact block (604-928-1361, jaredgibbons@royallepage.ca): the enquiry route on another firm's listing runs to Jared.
Census or demographic profile for this page: Not verified / not applicable — a search feed has no single geography; no census figure is stated and none was substituted.

items.t: The data route, as the page itself discloses it: Real estate listings held by participating real estate firms are marked with the MLS® logo and detailed information about the listing includes the name of the listing agent. This representation is based in whole or part on data generated by either the GVR, the FVREB or the CADREB which assumes no responsibility for its accuracy.

Reciprocity display rules: At the national level, CREA owns the MLS® and REALTOR® trademarks, and agents must be members of CREA and of a local real estate board — complying with both CREA's rules, including the REALTOR® Code, and their local board's rules — to access the MLS® system at all.

Feed mechanics: how listings are selected into this site's feed, how often it refreshes, why the count is 310 at reading, and whether sold or expired listings ever appear in it are not verified — the page text states no filter, no refresh interval beyond "real time"/"continuously" marketing language, and no inclusion rules.

Regulator — who you are dealing with: in British Columbia, real estate trading services are regulated by the BC Financial Services Authority (BCFSA), and BCFSA states a licensed professional must give consumers information about commissions and fees, must inform consumers of the duties owed to clients and non-clients, must inform unrepresented consumers of the risks of dealing with a professional representing another party, must disclose at the outset whether they can represent the consumer and how to complain to BCFSA, and can only work for either the buyer or the seller in a transaction — dual agency was prohibited in B.C. in 2018 except in the rarest of circumstances. That frame matters on this page precisely because the homes shown are other firms' listings: the agent whose contact block sits beside each card is not the listing agent.

blocks.text: Good to know about Recip

items.t: The slogan and the stamp disagree — use the stamp. The intro says "real time" and "updated continuously"; the feed stamps its own update time ("Data was last updated November 1, 2026 at 05:40 PM (UTC)").

The title and the editorial promise different geographies. The browser title says "Search all South Surrey listings" and the first page delivers exactly that (12 of 12 Surrey); the editorial below the feed promises Langley, Abbotsford and Chilliwack coverage the first page does not show.

Every first-page card is someone else's listing — by design. Eleven different brokerages name the 12 first-page cards and none is Jared's firm; the Reciprocity logo on each card is the tell. A buyer who assumes the contact block beside a card is the listing brokerage will misread who holds the listing.

Half the first page had an open house that weekend. Six of the 12 first-page cards carried open-house times for the November 1, 2026 weekend — the feed is a working open-house finder as a side effect, even though no separate open-houses function is stated on the page.
The boards disclaim their own feed.
No market number belongs to this page.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Recip

items.t: Scope note: the rules below are the frame for the Surrey ground the feed's first page displays, carried because a land buyer arriving via this search lands on Surrey parcels.
Surrey plans (for Surrey parcels): Surrey 2050 OCP Bylaw No. 21900 (adopted Jun 15, 2026) — current; Bylaw 18020 is REPLACED, never cite as current. Zoning Bylaw No. 12000.

SSMUH (Surrey, Jul 8, 2024): inside the urban containment boundary, on lots under 4,050 m² — 3 units (280 m² or less), 4 units (larger), up to 6 on eligible lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent bus stop. Added units are NOT subdivision permission.
Streamside (Surrey): setbacks in Part 7A of Zoning Bylaw 12000, varying by stream class — NO single riparian figure is ever stated.

STRs (Surrey): permitted, owner-only, owner must live at the property as primary residence; licence $358/yr carried with the City's $350/yr proposal disclosed as a CONFLICT — check the City licence page before quoting.

ALR block (for any ALR parcel a search surfaces): subdivision in the ALR needs ALC approval; residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha); farm class three-tier ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR.

BC strata block (bare-land strata lots included): Form B (within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports 5-year cycle for 5+ lots since Jul 1, 2024; min 10% CRF since Nov 1, 2023; rental bylaws VOID since Nov 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2 + May 1, 2023 exemptions); a "45+" line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw.

Programs attach to housing, not bare land: FTHB GST rebate (Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026 per CRA; 100% to $1M, max $50,000, phasing to $1.5M; agreements Mar 20, 2025–2031) — new HOUSING only. New Housing Rebate 36% / max $6,300 / $350K–$450K; HBP $60,000; FHSA $40,000 / $8,000/yr.

Consumer frame (BCFSA): a licensed professional must disclose whether they can represent the consumer, the duties owed to clients and non-clients, and the risks of dealing with a professional representing another party, and can work for either buyer or seller only (dual agency prohibited in BC in 2018 except in the rarest circumstances) — directly relevant here because the homes shown are other firms' listings.
